body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

The backup job editor is a wizard (General, Destination, Source data, Schedule, Options). A wizard helps the very first time, but a job is created once and edited many times. A typical edit touches one field (an exclude filter, the retention, the schedule), and I still have to step through the following pages to reach Save.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Make the five pages **tabs**: click any tab directly, and a **Save** button always visible.

For first-time users, the guidance doesn't need a wizard: a **guided tour** (product tour / coach marks, the bubbles that point at each field and move through the pages on their own, as done with libraries like Shepherd.js or Intro.js) can walk through the tabs on the first job, and can be skipped or replayed. That way the editor is fast for every later edit, and new users still get help.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Keeping the wizard only for new jobs and tabs when editing would already solve most of it. Today the only alternative is exporting, editing and importing the configuration, far more work for a one-field change.

**Additional context**

Duplicati 2.4.0.1, web UI.

comments.body:
Actually, that is how it secretly works.

You can click any step at the top to jump to it.
In edit mode, clicking "next" will save the edits.

The **Save changes** action is available in the published [Duplicati 2.4.1.101 Canary](https://github.com/duplicati/duplicati/releases/tag/v2.4.1.101_canary_2026-11-07): I confirmed that the official Windows package contains the button and its save handler, so you can check this workflow with that Canary release.
For clarity, my live verification used a production build of the **latest ngclient main UI** at [`f217ce91146c6be358f054f32f030e2503ad3005`](https://github.com/duplicati/ngclient/commit/f217ce91146c6be358f054f32f030e2503ad3005), connected to an isolated Windows **2.4.1.101 Canary server**; it did not use the UI bundled with the release.
With that main UI, I could jump directly between all five existing-job editor pages and use **Save changes** on each without advancing through the remaining steps; saving stayed on the current page. A description changed on General survived jumping directly to Options, saving and reloading; API readback also confirmed that the destination URL and an existing advanced option were retained. Related tests passed: `e2e/editor-save.spec.ts` (5), `backup.editor-save.spec.ts` (8), and the production build.
Could you please recheck with **2.4.1.101 Canary** and let us know whether this addresses your editing workflow? The navigation is still visually presented as wizard steps: are tab styling, a guided tour, or other parts of the original request still needed?

body:
If the editor (say destination config) is somehow broken, it will mess up the connection string on edit/save.
This happens because the event flow is triggered once the path is initially set.
The string is then decoded into forms, and once the form is populated, it is serialized back.

The effect of this is that the string is changed, even if the user has not actively changed anything.
If the user then saves the backup (or simply navigates) the incorrect string is written to the config.

comments.body:
Verified on main [626f10a35876753f0a2f36d414c878c91a819067](https://github.com/duplicati/ngclient/commit/626f10a35876753f0a2f36d414c878c91a819067).

#618 addresses the load/serialize feedback loop by preserving the saved URL and applying only explicit edits. Verified scope: I reran `destination-edit-session.spec.ts` and `single-destination.render.spec.ts`; both passed, covering untouched URL values, unknown/repeated query parameters, credentials, and parse/mapper failures across their regression cases.

These are unit/component checks, not live connection tests for every provider. Is there a specific editor or configuration that still loses settings, or another remaining case you would like covered here?


Since Chromium based browsers have most of the market, I don't know why reports of this problem aren't numerous.

[The connection to the server is lost when using Firefox #396](https://github.com/duplicati/ngclient/issues/396)
reports a similar problem, but in the opposite direction. For me, Edge (and Chrome) consistently fail on morning PC wake.

> If the token expires, the websocket can fail to authenticate Because I'm tired of constant failures overnight (even in Chrome) I tried [below](https://forum.duplicati.com/t/release-2-1-0-119-canary-2025-05-29/20715#p-77809-disabling-reported-options-on-webserver-9), which has had a few forum mentions. `--webservice-disable-api-extensions so websocket usage can be disabled` More specifically, TrayIcon has `--webservice-disable-api-extensions=v1:websocket` as was mentioned in forum [here](https://forum.duplicati.com/t/disable-password-on-gui/19638/35?u=ts678): ``` You can try to disable the websocket by starting Duplicati with: --webservice-disable-api-extensions=v1:websocket This will instruct ngclient to fall back to the polling method ``` It still doesn't connect backup without manual refresh, but at least my profiling log stays quiet. No token complaints. ngclient is doing its countdown (is this shorter than usual?) from 5 to 1 and then back to 5, displaying this in window: 2.2.0.1_stable_2025-11-09

2.2.0.101_canary_2025-11-20 has been running here since Nov 20, but I did a rare restart sequence of Windows, Duplicati, Chrome.

[Release: 2.2.0.101 (Canary) 2025-11-20](https://forum.duplicati.com/t/release-2-2-0-101-canary-2025-11-20/21656/17?u=ts678) has its story. In dev tools or log file it's different than the usual one about an expired token.

> `ws://127.0.0.1:8101/notifications`

> `{"Version":1,"Token":"PROXY_AUTHED_FAKE_TOKEN"}`

> `Microsoft.IdentityModel.Tokens.SecurityTokenMalformedException: IDX12741: JWT must have three segments (JWS) or five segments (JWE).`

I verified this in Chromium using ngclient main [`20d6c2128e6c5166ced84784385064b7ff788157`](https://github.com/duplicati/ngclient/commit/20d6c2128e6c5166ced84784385064b7ff788157) against an isolated Windows server running Duplicati `2.4.1.101_canary_2026-11-07`. I let the access token expire and injected a single HTTP 503 on the first refresh request in each test. The retry succeeded in both cases.

- **WebSocket:** After a forced disconnect, the server rejected the expired token with `4401`. The client refreshed the token and received server status, notifications, and the backup list again without reloading the page.
- **Long polling:** With WebSocket disabled, the poll received `401`. After the token refresh succeeded, a subsequent poll returned `200` and the page reflected the server state change without a reload.

@ts678, could you retest the disconnect you saw with a current build and let us know whether the page still gets stuck? If it now recovers without a reload in your setup too, I suggest closing this issue.

body:
If remote files are damaged or missing, Duplicati needs to remove the affected files from the backups.

This is done by first calling "list-broken-files" which will show the files and versions that can no longer be restored.
After the user accepts, the API for purge-broken-files should be called.

comments.body:
Making this more visible in the GUI may cause questions about what sorts of damage can be detected.
I'm pretty sure things like corrupted files detected by download (e.g. `test`) must be manually deleted.
That functionality is beyond the GUI, but the GUI (and documentation) decide how to phrase promises.

I verified the list and purge flow in Chromium on ngclient main [`20d6c2128e6c5166ced84784385064b7ff788157`](https://github.com/duplicati/ngclient/commit/20d6c2128e6c5166ced84784385064b7ff788157) against an isolated Windows server running Duplicati `2.4.1.101_canary_2026-11-07`.

- I removed one data volume used only by the newer of two backup versions. The UI listed the affected entries. Opening the list and opening or cancelling the confirmation left the destination file hashes and backup catalog unchanged, with no purge request sent.
- After confirming, the purge completed and the broken-file list was empty. The unaffected older version kept its original timestamp, and its restored file matched the original byte for byte.

This covers a missing data volume in a local test repository. Other forms of corruption, including damage detected by downloading a volume, were outside this test. Would it make sense to close this issue as implemented?

title: Create a list-broken-files and purge-broken-files page

body:
For manual maintenance of the backups it is sometimes needed to delete versions of the backups.

To implement this we simply need to list the versions (see the restore flow for how to get them).
Each version is then displayed with a number (1 is the newest), a timestamp, total size, and total filecount (all from the same API call).
A checkbox is show for each version, and an overall checkbox for "Compact afterwards".

The call should then take the timestamps for all the checked versions and send them to the API (endpoint is missing from client).

comments.body:
Verified on main [626f10a35876753f0a2f36d414c878c91a819067](https://github.com/duplicati/ngclient/commit/626f10a35876753f0a2f36d414c878c91a819067).

Verified scope: the production UI in Chromium lists version metadata and supports selection and the compact option. With mocked API responses, selecting version 0 and disabling compaction sent nothing before confirmation, then sent `{ "BackupId": "42", "Versions": [0], "SuppressCompact": true }`. The related component tests also passed; I did not perform an actual server-side deletion.

The requested UI appears implemented. The current V2 endpoint uses version IDs rather than the timestamps mentioned originally. Would it make sense to close this issue as implemented?

I followed up with an end-to-end check in Chromium using ngclient main [`20d6c2128e6c5166ced84784385064b7ff788157`](https://github.com/duplicati/ngclient/commit/20d6c2128e6c5166ced84784385064b7ff788157) against an isolated Windows server running Duplicati `2.4.1.101_canary_2026-11-07`.

- In each of two three-version backups, selecting and deleting version 1 removed only the middle version. The oldest and newest versions kept their original timestamps and their distinct files.
- With **Compact after deletion** off, `SuppressCompact: true` skipped compaction and all 23 data volumes remained. With it on, `SuppressCompact: false` ran compaction and reduced the data volumes from 23 to 2.

Would it make sense to close this issue as implemented?
